# Snowman ⛄

Guess the word, one letter at a time.

Every wrong letter melts part of the snowman!

Press **↓** to play.

::: notes
Tap the letters on the board, or type them on the keyboard. **💡 Hint** shows the picture and the meaning.

To make your own: `{{{< snowman "democracy" >}}}` (a vocab word), `{{{< snowman "Parthenon" hint="..." image="images/..." >}}}` (your own word), or `{{{< snowman unit=1 >}}}` (a random word from the unit, with a **🔀 New word** button). These slides go down (↓): a word, then a slide about it, then the next word.
:::

## Word 1

{{< snowman "democracy" >}}

## Democracy

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- {{< vocab "democracy" text="Democracy" >}}: the people decide.
- In Athens, {{< vocab "citizen" text="citizens" >}} met in the {{< vocab "assembly" >}}.
- They {{< vocab "vote" text="voted" >}} on laws by raising their hands.
- Only free men born in Athens could vote.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](images/GRC-003.svg){fig-alt="Drawing of people raising their hands to vote"}
:::
::::

## Word 2

{{< snowman "Parthenon" hint="A famous temple in Athens, for the goddess Athena." image="images/parthenon-west.jpg" >}}

## The Parthenon

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A {{< vocab "temple" >}} for **Athena**, the goddess of Athens.
- It stands on a hill called the **Acropolis**.
- The Greeks built it from white marble, from 447 to 432 BC.
- It has rows of tall {{< vocab "column" text="columns" >}}.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/parthenon-west.jpg){.photo fig-alt="The Parthenon, a ruined marble temple with rows of columns, under a blue sky"}
:::
::::

# Picture reveal 🖼️

A picture is hiding under the tiles.

Open one tile at a time. Who can guess it first?

Press **↓** to play.

::: notes
Fewer tiles opened = a better guess. Tap **Show the answer** when someone gets it.

To make your own: `{{{< picture-reveal "aqueduct" >}}}` (a vocab word's picture), `{{{< picture-reveal "Parthenon" image="images/parthenon-west.jpg" >}}}` (your own picture), or `{{{< picture-reveal unit=1 >}}}` (random, with **🔀 New picture**). Add `tiles=9` or `tiles=25` for fewer or more tiles.
:::

# Jeopardy 🏆

Choose a category and a number.

Bigger numbers are harder questions.

Press **↓** to play.

::: notes
Teams take turns choosing a square. Read the clue, give the team time to answer, then tap **Show the answer**.

To make your own board, write a list: each category in **bold**, and under it one line per clue: the clue, a `|`, then the answer. The first clue is worth 100, the next 200, and so on. `{{{< jeopardy unit=1 >}}}` makes a board from the unit's vocab instead, with **🔀 New board**.
:::

## Ancient Greece

::: {.jeopardy}
- **Places**
  - Land with water on three sides | a peninsula
  - This city had the first democracy | Athens
  - Boys here left home at 7 to train as soldiers | Sparta
  - The Olympic Games were held here | Olympia
- **Gods**
  - The king of the gods | Zeus
  - The goddess of wisdom | Athena
  - The god of the sea | Poseidon
  - The gods lived on this mountain | Mount Olympus
- **Buildings**
  - A tall post that holds up a roof | a column
  - A building for a god or goddess | a temple
  - A famous temple in Athens | the Parthenon
  - An outdoor place for plays | a theater
- **Ideas**
  - People choose by raising their hands | vote
  - A story about gods and heroes | a myth
  - A thinker who asks big questions | a philosopher
  - Sports contests to honor Zeus | the Olympic Games
:::

# Quick-fire ⚡

A question pops up. Answer fast!

The teacher points to you. Say the answer out loud.

Press **↓** to play.

::: notes
Point to a student, let them answer, then tap **Show the answer** and mark it **✓ Right** or **✗ Wrong**. The game keeps the score.

To make your own: `::: {.trivia title="..." seconds="10"}`, then one line per question: the question, a `|`, then the answer (one or two words is best). `seconds="0"` turns the timer off. `{{{< trivia unit=1 >}}}` asks about the unit's vocab instead, with **🔀 New questions**.
:::

## Greece review

::: {.trivia title="Ancient Greece review" seconds="10"}
- Which city had the first democracy? | Athens
- Greek stories about gods and heroes are called… | myths
- The Olympic Games honored which god? | Zeus
- Which city-state trained boys to be soldiers? | Sparta
- What is land with water on three sides? | a peninsula
:::
